findings.where: resources/workflow-graph/workflow-graph.v1.json t_556 (accept_staging -> integrate_staging, guard_560 authority actor=human) and t_557/guard_561; 01-core-flows.md:298,306 (§7 preamble, step 5); docs/contracts/integration-authorization.md:12 (§1.2); src/host/staging-acceptance.mjs:441-458 (autoPolicyAcceptance)
findings.what: The pinned auto-policy path is normative but has no way to run. 01 §7, IA §1 and autoPolicyAcceptance say a record signed for a pinned auto-policy 'before this step' lets the flow skip the human stop at accept_staging. But the only graph edges out of accept_staging toward the CAS (t_556) and delivery (t_557) carry guard authority actor=human. The graph uses actor=policy elsewhere, so this is a choice, not a gap in the vocabulary. After R7-15 the policy's pinned_identity and the record must bind the staging identity, which binds aggregate_record_hash and so exists only after aggregate_verify. The flow goes straight from aggregate_verify to accept_staging, and no step, packet or park presents that identity for signing in between. Any signature can therefore only come at the human stop itself, and the graph's authority would refuse a policy actor there anyway. An implementer of #18's guard-authority evaluator and an implementer of autoPolicyAcceptance would build incompatible things. Fix: either give t_556/t_557 a policy-authority guard plus a step or packet where the user signs the post-aggregate identity, or drop the auto-policy path for Epics.

findings.where: docs/contracts/integration-authorization.md:11,15,34,43; 01-core-flows.md:128,249,298; 02-architecture.md:431; 03-technical-plan.md:364,1007; src/host/staging-acceptance.mjs:44 HEAD_FACTS, 380-383
findings.what: It is undefined whether the acceptance's own UserDecisionRecord changes the heads the authorization binds. The IA record and the staging identity bind relevant_authority_projection_hash, dependency_head_hash and intent_head_hash as 'the heads the signature was made against' (IA §3), all composed before the question. Creating the signing UserDecisionRecord commits authority and nonce heads (01 §2). The dependency projection is defined as 'current authority/policy/waiver IDs' of the Epic (01 §5). integrateApproved then checks that the named heads are 'the ones in force' (IA §1, 03 integrate_staging). No document says whether an integration-acceptance record of this Epic enters its relevant authority projection or dependency head. If it does, every Epic authorization is acceptance_stale at integrate_staging by construction. If it does not, the exclusion is unstated on the one irreversible step. Fix: state the rule, e.g. that integration-acceptance records are excluded from the relevant projection, or that integrateApproved compares the pre-acceptance heads the record names.

findings.where: 01-core-flows.md:294 (§6 'Лимит полного цикла — 10 раундов') and :397 (§9 'cap ограничивает автономные раунды абсолютно'); workflow-graph.v1.json caps (only t_231 narrow_review_join->fix_artifact, t_443 record_code_verdict->fix); t_205 synthesize_panel->fix_artifact (guard_212/cond_110), t_187/t_188 freeze_artifact->dispatch_panel (cond_092/cond_093); docs/contracts/workflow-factory.md:105-107
findings.what: The review cap is stated as absolute but counts only narrow re-review rounds and the code verdict->fix edge. A full-panel NOT_PASS goes synthesize_panel -> fix_artifact (t_205), which no cap counts. If the fix changes scope or load-bearing decisions, cond_093 routes freeze_artifact -> dispatch_panel for another full four-model panel, and so on. A sequence of full-panel rounds, the most expensive kind, therefore never reaches review_cap, and neither does the verify->fix repair loop (t_416). ADR-099 fixed the decision half of R7-4 but not what the counter covers. Fix: count t_205 as well, e.g. with a second cap on the artifact_review_round reason, or narrow the wording in 01 §6/§9 to 'narrow re-review rounds'.

ADR-101 notes the unregistered_artifact/unknown_class split as candidate debt, but the package does not, and nobody addressed the missing recovery row.

findings.where: docs/contracts/platform-support.md:53 (§5: autoskd is one of three binaries 'owned by the installing user') and :61-67 (§5a: git writers = autosk-flow-ref-custody and autoskd; 'the installing user's own account no longer writes the project's .git directly, and neither does a model's'); resources/platform-support/platform-support.v1.json:157,183-187 (git_directory_writers [ref-custody, autoskd], user_account_git_writes=false; no account field for autoskd or for model processes); 02-architecture.md:67 ('Project/model accounts cannot open either Git directory for writes or invoke Git mutations; autoskd mediates'); matrix.v1.json:385 (#13 obligation: 'leaves the user's account no direct write to the project's .git'); compat/autosk/patches/0028-session-bound-create.patch:1064-1126 (autoskEnv: model processes are spawned by autoskd; no setuid/credential drop anywhere in the 49 patches); 02 §1 (host Git commands run via ctx.exec in the daemon: delta-driver.mjs:115-242, execution-base-driver.mjs:74-87, planning-driver.mjs:105, aggregate-driver.mjs:52 'worktree add')
findings.what: Debt 11a's install record gives only the ref-custody helper a separate account. It makes autoskd a writer of the project's .git while denying writes to the user's account and the model's. No record, obligation or patch gives autoskd or model processes an account of their own. autoskd is a §5 installing-user binary. Every host Git write (update-index, write-tree, commit-tree, worktree add) runs in the daemon through ctx.exec. Model processes are autoskd's children with no uid drop anywhere in the series, and no sandbox mechanism is in the platform contract or the matrix. So autoskd writes .git as the user's uid, which contradicts user_account_git_writes=false. Or else autoskd cannot write at all, and the host drivers and integrateApproved cannot run. Either way, a model subprocess holds the same OS rights as autoskd. The helper account still protects refs/autosk/**. But 'target ref moves only by the daemon's integrateApproved under a signed IntegrationAuthorizationRecord' has no enforcing mechanism: a model can `git update-ref refs/heads/<target>`. An implementer of #13 following §5a would build exactly this topology. This is round-7 R7-3's gap narrowed, not closed, and package §5 does not name it.

findings.where: resources/clean-room-e2e/fault-matrix.v1.json:50-55 (F002), :77-82 (F003); docs/contracts/clean-room-e2e.md:84-90, :101; package §5 fault table (F002/F003 'real_path', detected yes)
findings.what: F002 designs 'kill the daemon, restart, repeat the same creation key', and F003 designs 'SIGKILL between the transcript header and the meta write'. Each injection_note says the run does neither: the daemon is never killed or restarted, and no transcript or meta write is involved. Both still reach covered_without_control. The coverage rule reads only injection kind, detection and control, and never whether the injected fault is the designed one. So if a control is added under #36, both groups count toward the release gate as covered_by_real_fault while the designed faults stay unexercised. Fix: a state (or a validator refusal) for a group whose injection_note departs from its fault, excluded from the gate.

findings.where: 01-core-flows.md:380; src/host/staging-acceptance.mjs:429-457 (autoPolicyAcceptance comment: 'in advance means before this acceptance step, for this exact identity — which exists only once the aggregate has passed'); docs/contracts/epic-staging.md:104

findings.where: docs/contracts/platform-support.md:51-53 (§5) vs :61-67 (§5a); resources/platform-support/platform-support.v1.json:155-187 (install.binaries; ref_custody_service.git_directory_writers=[autosk-flow-ref-custody, autoskd], user_account_git_writes=false); 02-architecture.md:67,71; docs/contracts/epic-planning-ref.md:183,211; README.md rule 19; 04-decisions.md ADR-095 (l.1154)
findings.what: The custody boundary's account model contradicts itself, and README rule 19 tells the user something the design cannot deliver. §5a and the install record allow two writers of the project's .git, the ref-custody service account and autoskd, and say the installing user's account, and the model's, never write it. But only the helper gets its own account (runs_as=dedicated_service_account). autoskd is one of §5's three binaries 'owned by the installing user', with no runs_as field, and the model processes are spawned by autoskd (pi-agent, claude-agent) under its uid. 02 §2 and epic-planning-ref.md deny writes to 'project/model accounts', but no install record, platform row, matrix obligation or ADR creates a model account or a daemon account. Unix permissions are per uid, so 'autoskd writes .git' and 'the user's account does not' cannot both hold, and the models inherit whichever is true. The 'autoskd mediates ordinary project Git operations' surface, which the host drivers (commit-tree and hash-object -w in planning-driver.mjs:105,121, delta-driver.mjs:242, execution-base-driver.mjs:87) and every implementer step rely on, is also in no preflight primitive, no matrix owner and no patch. An implementer following #13's obligation either locks autoskd out of the ODB or leaves the user and every model with direct .git write, and the second defeats the sole-writer and staging_moved_after_pass guarantees ADR-095 rests on. Fix: an install record for the autoskd and model-process accounts (or group model), with an owner for the Git-mediation surface, or narrow rule 19 and §5a to what one uid can enforce.

findings.where: src/host/staging-acceptance.mjs:44-49,101-104,229-231,341-345; docs/contracts/integration-authorization.md §3 ('the heads the signature was made against'), §5; 03-technical-plan.md:364 (integrateApproved re-checks the named heads), :1007 ('Unrelated project authority append therefore does not stale an Epic'); 01-core-flows.md §2 ('Daemon commits authority+nonce heads before returning record/projection/effects'), §5 (dependency projection = current authority/policy/waiver IDs), §2 ('the same channel is required for … integration acceptance')
findings.what: Debt 11b (ADR-096) makes the staging identity and the IntegrationAuthorizationRecord bind relevant_authority_projection_hash, dependency_head_hash and intent_head_hash as they stand before the question. The record's validity then depends on the very act that signs it. The person's acceptance is an Epic-scoped UserDecisionRecord (epic_id set) in the authority journal, and the daemon commits the authority head before it returns the record. 03:1007 exempts only unrelated appends from staling an Epic, and no text excludes an Epic's own acceptance decision, or the record it completes, from the Epic's relevant projection. On that reading, the heads in force after the signature differ from the ones the record names. acceptanceFromDecision rebuilds the identity from the heads in force and compares it with the one asked (acceptance_stale), and integrateApproved compares the named heads with the ones in force. So every acceptance goes stale on the one irreversible path, and each re-ask repeats the loop. The fix is local: define the relevant projection so it excludes the acceptance decision itself, or compare the heads as of that decision's previous_secure_head_hash. Nothing does either today, and an implementer following 03 literally builds a CAS that is never admitted.

findings.where: src/host/delta-driver.mjs applyDelta (readRef must equal base.commit_oid → foreign_ref_movement; commit-tree with no recorded recipe or expected OID; askCustody request carries no operation id); src/host/ref-custody.mjs formRequest ({action, ref_updates} only); resources/planning-publication/ref-custody-helper-intents.schema.json:17 (intent requires owner_operation_id, request_id); 02-architecture.md §2 ('Retry looks up that intent and journal rather than minting a second request'); docs/contracts/epic-staging.md §7 (recovery only after aggregate PASS), §9 ('a crash before and after each staging apply'); graph apply_staging reasons (receipt_missing, delta_stale; no foreign_ref_movement)
findings.what: The host↔daemon custody boundary loses the operation identity a crash-safe staging apply needs. The host's request to the daemon's helper client has no operation or request id, while the daemon-side intent it must persist requires owner_operation_id. The delta commit is written with no persisted recipe or expected OID, unlike the planning adapter. The retry path refuses a staging ref not at the base with foreign_ref_movement, a code no graph edge carries. The result: if the helper has committed advance_staging and the host crashes before the integration receipt, the retry cannot recognise its own commit, re-forms a different request, and parks receipt_missing. That row's required state ('receipt и lineage восстановлены') has no mechanism to restore anything, and epic-staging §7 describes recovery only for the post-aggregate crash. Fix: persist an apply recipe with its expected commit OID and operation id before asking, pass the id across the boundary, and treat staging at the expected commit as an apply already done.

findings.where: 01-core-flows.md §7 preamble and step 5; 04-decisions.md ADR-096 (R7-15 decision); src/host/staging-acceptance.mjs:429-457 autoPolicyAcceptance; workflow-graph.v1.json accept_staging conditions (lines ~3293-3321, 16919)
findings.what: R7-15 was closed by redefining 'signed in advance' as 'before the acceptance step, for the exact identity'. That identity exists only after aggregate_verify, and the graph goes straight on to accept_staging. No step, packet or channel between those two steps presents the composed record to the user for signature; acceptancePacket is the stop itself. The pinned auto-policy path, which the design says lets the flow skip the human stop, therefore has no producer of its signed record except an out-of-band race. It fails closed, but it is a described mechanism that does not exist. Either add a pre-acceptance signing packet or state that the auto-policy only removes the wait after a signature made at the stop.

findings.where: src/host/user-decision.mjs:156-158 resumeDecisionSubject, :179-192 resumeDecisionAdmitter
findings.what: The resume-decision subject binds task_id, reason, watermark and target, but not the project. The admitter never compares record.project_root_sha256 with the resuming project; it only checks that the field is present. Isolation between projects for decision-gated resumes (a review round past review_cap) therefore rests on the store lookup location and on task ids never colliding between projects, rather than on the signed identity. That is weaker than 02 §5's rule that artifact/PASS bindings include project identity.

findings.where: src/host/staging-acceptance.mjs:161-175 composeAuthorization (previousAuthorizationHeadHash from the caller); docs/contracts/integration-authorization.md §3 (host cannot check the chain); 02-architecture.md §5 (integration_authorization_head in the secure store, scope unstated)
findings.what: The user signs previous_authorization_head_hash as the host was handed it, and the host cannot read the head. The documents do not say whether integration_authorization_head is per scope or per project. If it is per project, any other Epic's or Quick run's record stored between question and CAS makes this record's chain stale at integrateApproved, which forces a fresh human signature. That is a liveness coupling between Epics the one-CAS serialization text (ADR-099) does not name.
